payload.problem_addressed: Geometric and topological anomalies (self-intersections, edge collapses, disconnected vertices) in intermediate wireframes of multi-stage B-Rep generation pipelines propagate to invalid final B-Reps, and retraining large generative models to fix this is computationally prohibitive.
payload.method_summary: WDR (Wireframe Detection and Repair) is a training-free framework that intervenes at the intermediate wireframe stage of B-Rep generation. A Geometric-Topology Anomaly Detector (GTAD) combines parallel VLM-based coarse screening with geometric and topological detectors to predict downstream invalidity risk and route generation to dedicated repair branches. An Energy-Guided Geometric-Topology Repair (EGGTR) module then performs detector-triggered guided regeneration through geometry and topology branches, scaling test-time computation via Energy-Guided Resampling and training-free guidance for diffusion models.
payload.contributions_summary: The paper proposes WDR, a training-free framework that detects and repairs geometric/topological anomalies at the intermediate wireframe stage of multi-stage B-Rep CAD generation, avoiding costly retraining of the underlying generative model. It combines a VLM-based and geometric/topological anomaly detector (GTAD) with an energy-guided repair module (EGGTR) that can plug into both autoregressive and diffusion CAD pipelines without retraining. Experiments show consistent improvements in kernel-checked B-Rep validity while largely preserving the diversity and distributional quality of generated CAD models.
key_architecture_choices: Training-free, plug-in intervention at the intermediate wireframe stage rather than end-to-end retraining
Geometric-Topology Anomaly Detector (GTAD): parallel VLM-based coarse screening + geometric/topological detectors
Energy-Guided Geometric-Topology Repair (EGGTR): detector-triggered guided regeneration via geometry and topology branches
Energy-Guided Resampling and training-free guidance for diffusion models to scale test-time compute
metrics: measured diversity / distributional quality of synthesized CAD models
payload.headline_results: Consistent improvements in kernel-checked validity of generated B-Reps while largely retaining the diversity and distributional quality of the synthesized CAD models, as integrated into both autoregressive and diffusion CAD generation pipelines.
claimed_advantages: Training-free: no retraining of the large upstream generative model needed
Works as a drop-in intervention compatible with both autoregressive and diffusion CAD pipelines
Improves downstream B-Rep validity without materially sacrificing diversity/distributional quality
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: Directly relevant to STRUCTURAL VALIDITY: WDR's core idea -- detect geometric/topological anomalies in an intermediate representation and trigger targeted, guided repair/regeneration rather than retraining -- is a candidate mechanism to add on top of our verifier-guided best-of-N screening. In hexgen, an analogous 'detect-then-repair' pass could operate on partially-generated block/sweep/projection programs (or their intermediate geometric state) before full execution, potentially reducing wasted verifier calls on doomed candidates and providing a cheaper alternative/complement to full rejection sampling. The GTAD detector-routing idea (route to a dedicated repair branch based on predicted invalidity risk) also parallels our frozen verifier's role, and could inspire a lightweight risk-predictor that pre-screens candidates before the expensive verifier pass.
payload.reviewer_notes: Only the abstract was available in this harvest (no body chunks), so architecture/dataset/metric details beyond the abstract are unknown -- 'code will be made publicly available upon acceptance' but no link is given yet, and the paper appears to be a preprint/submission, not yet peer-reviewed. Worth a follow-up read once the full text or code lands, since 'wireframe' here is a CAD-generation intermediate representation, not the hexgen DSL program itself, so the repair mechanism would need adaptation rather than direct reuse.
payload.implementation_cost_estimate: M (would require adapting the detect-and-repair idea to hexgen's program/verifier setup; no code available yet)
